clusters.name: Failed or stalled runs fail silently: nobody gets told
clusters.pain: When an unattended run errors or a sub-agent hangs, there is no failure signal. Founders find out from a missing report, a daily console check, or a coordinator that waits forever.
clusters.fix: Add failure notifications to deployments: webhook events for session failed/errored/terminated, plus a default idle timeout on multiagent sub-threads that raises a thread.idle_timeout error to the coordinator and fires the same webhook, instead of waiting forever. Ship it with a short doc recipe, "Get pinged when a scheduled run fails".

clusters.name: Recurring runs repeat stale work: no per-run 'today' and no memory of earlier runs
clusters.pain: Scheduled runs don't know what changed since the last run. They either replay a frozen input (a hardcoded date) or forget what earlier runs already handled, so the same stale output comes back every day and trust erodes.
clusters.fix: Have deployments inject run context into every session they start (scheduled_for, run_number, last_successful_run_at) so task text never hardcodes a date. Document it in a "Designing a recurring agent" guide that separates per-run inputs (from run context) from persistent state (a memory store of items already handled, e.g. carriers already escalated).

clusters.name: Can't reconstruct what a run did, which agent did it, or what it cost
clusters.pain: After a bad run, founders rebuild the story by hand, from interleaved raw logs or by matching output against the bill. They can't see per-agent steps or per-run cost.
clusters.fix: Tag every session event with thread_id and agent name, and add a running cost/token total to the event stream. Support filtering by thread and a per-thread last-step and wait-state summary, so "which agent stalled, on what step, and what did this run cost" is answered by one API call rather than by reading raw logs.

clusters.name: No obvious place for API keys, so they end up in the prompt
clusters.pain: Founders connecting a third-party API can't find where a credential should live, so they paste it into the prompt or stop to ask.
clusters.fix: Write a "Where do API keys go?" vault quickstart: store the key in a vault, reference it from the MCP connector or tool config, and never put it in the prompt. Link it from the agent-creation page, and make the agent/session create API return a warning with that link when it sees a key-shaped string in a system prompt or task.

clusters.name: No way to score agent quality over time or across changes
clusters.pain: After changing instructions, founders can't tell whether output got better or worse. They eyeball a couple of outputs and have no numbers.
clusters.fix: Persist outcome grader scores per session, keyed by agent version, with a list/aggregate endpoint (score by version over time). Ship an "eval harness" skill that replays a fixed input set against two agent versions and reports the score delta.

clusters.name: Runaway run: no spend cap or stopping point
clusters.pain: A self-directed run kept going with no budget and no completion criterion, and cost more than the previous week in one go. The founder turned the agent off.
clusters.fix: Make a per-session budget cap the default on scheduled deployments (opt out, not opt in), with a webhook at 80% and at the cap. Document pairing it with an outcome stop criterion (e.g. "draft with 5-6 items written") so the run ends when the job is done.

clusters.name: Agent can't reach data inside the company's private network (VPC)
clusters.pain: The cloud-hosted agent can't reach a database inside the VPC. Opening the database to the internet is unacceptable, and manual exports defeat the purpose.
clusters.fix: Publish a "Reach a database inside your VPC" guide with a reference self-hosted MCP server. It runs inside the VPC, makes outbound connections only, and exposes a narrow read-only tool (e.g. fetch_flagged_transactions(week)) rather than raw SQL. DB credentials go in a vault, and the environment's network is limited to that connector.

clusters.name: Can't get output files out of a finished session
clusters.pain: The agent reports that it wrote a file to outputs, but the founder can't work out how to download it after the session ends. The docs' mention of "scope" doesn't help.
clusters.fix: Add an end-to-end "Get files out of a session" example to the files API docs: agent writes to outputs, then list the session's files, then download after the session ends. Explain file scope (session-scoped vs persisted) in plain language, with the exact call for each.

clusters.name: Sandbox dependency setup eats the first day
clusters.pain: Common Python packages are missing from the sandbox, and installing them times out.
clusters.fix: Let environments declare packages (a requirements list) that are installed once at environment build and cached across sessions, with a longer install timeout. Preinstall common data libraries (pandas, numpy) in the default image.

clusters.name: Must have a human approve before the agent acts externally
clusters.pain: A hard requirement, not a failure. In regulated work nothing can leave without a human reading it, and the founder must be able to explain what the agent did.
clusters.fix: Publish a "Draft, then approve" pattern doc and skill: a permission policy with no outbound-send tool (or one that requires human confirmation), the deliverable written as a draft file via the files API, and an outcome defined as "draft ready for review" rather than "sent".
clusters.uncounted_support: Mentor observation notion-006 (unnamed teams, not counted) says the same theme recurs across teams. Priya's definition of done also keeps the final send with her, but she did not raise it as a problem, so she is not counted.

quotes.text: anything touching our data or our regulator has to be something I can explain and stand behind.
quotes.author: Aisha (Ledgerline)
